page: OVHcloud b2-120 is a general-purpose server powered by an Intel x86_64 processor based on the Haswell architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores with one thread per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 120 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core, and includes 400 GB of local SSD storage. Network connectivity is supported by a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the instance runs on a KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate a significant divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance is poor, falling into the bottom 10% in stress-ng tests, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak. However, the server achieves average performance in multi-core CPU benchmarks, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth, both cached and uncached, remains in the average tier, as do Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput.

From a resource density perspective, the b2-120 offers a high physical core count without hyperthreading, which eliminates resource contention between threads on the same core. However, the older Intel Haswell architecture represents a clear tradeoff, resulting in lower single-core efficiency compared to modern processors. This makes the server less cost-effective for single-threaded applications but highly suitable for parallelized workloads that can leverage all 32 dedicated cores.

This server is best suited for multi-threaded general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, database operations, and parallelized data processing. It is also appropriate for moderate Redis deployments and multi-threaded compression tasks, whereas it is not recommended for single-threaded applications or intensive LLM text generation.
